record.original_question: Does every triangular billiard admit at least one periodic trajectory?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Do all triangular billiards have some periodic trajectory?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the billiard dynamical system inside a triangle T in the Euclidean plane: a point particle moves in straight lines inside T and reflects off each side according to the law of equal angles (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection); trajectories that hit a vertex are undefined. A trajectory is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial direction.

Question: Does every triangle T in the plane admit at least one periodic billiard trajectory?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a well-known open question. Periodic trajectories are known to exist in all acute triangles (Fagnano), all right triangles (Holt, 1993), and—via computer-assisted proofs by Schwartz and others—in all obtuse triangles with maximum angle at most about 112.5°, as well as in obtuse triangles whose smallest angle is at least 11° (with limited exceptions). The general case for arbitrary obtuse triangles remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Triangular billiards - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether or not in every obtuse triangle a periodic billiard trajectory exists.
status_evidence.claim: The general existence of periodic trajectories in every triangle remains open.

status_evidence.title: Obtuse Triangular Billiards II: 100 Degrees Worth of Periodic Trajectories
status_evidence.snippet: Computer-assisted proof showing all obtuse triangles with maximum angle at most ~112.5° admit periodic billiard paths.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results cover obtuse triangles up to ~112.5°.

status_evidence.title: On Periodic Billiard Trajectories in Obtuse Triangles
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on the existence question for periodic billiard trajectories in obtuse triangles.
status_evidence.claim: The question is recognized as a long-standing open problem.
